second_order: staging and working out the Kubo April Fools makeover
theme_note: These codes hold together because people enact and interpret the room's own April Fools joke: they test suspicious announcements, replace ordinary Zootopia formats with Kubo, perform shock or devotion, play along, object, and explain the joke. What varies is whether a turn stages the joke, is confused by it, or makes it explicit. This is subreddit conduct, not canvas conduct.

second_order: getting Predditors onto one pixel-art job
theme_note: These codes coordinate attention and placements around a shared job by proposing it, explaining how to contribute, fixing one location, giving it scarce sticky space, or redirecting readers to the work thread. What varies is the organizing device: instructions, location, pinning, or referral.

second_order: building and extending Nick, Judy, and the sign
theme_note: These codes report or direct additions to the shared picture itself. What varies is the stage of making: finishing Nick, moving to Judy, or adding the collective signature.

These codes hold together as hands-on repair: people report lost work, spend placements undoing obscene changes, and put repairs before spare help. What varies is whether the damage is disappearance, deliberate vandalism, or competing demand on a placement.

second_order: working out room and help with neighbours
theme_note: These codes negotiate coexistence around the picture: asking to accommodate another work, refusing to move Judy, proposing another location, trying to preserve both pictures, or asking a neighbour for help. What varies is who asks, whether the issue is space or spare placements, and whether the answer is refusal, relocation, or compromise.

second_order: showing and celebrating the picture taking shape
theme_note: These codes make the emerging result visible and meaningful to the room by showing a find, celebrating subreddits leaving a mark, or noticing Judy beside Nick. What varies is whether the turn displays, celebrates, or recognizes progress.

second_order: arguing over what belongs in the shared picture
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants contest or seek agreement over visible design choices rather than merely repairing damage. In this slice the variation is Judy's foot colour, the heart between Nick and Judy, and whether changes require a room-wide discussion.

second_order: handing maintenance to a bot and its template
theme_note: These codes describe people reorganizing upkeep through a bot: starting it, privately lending accounts, expanding its reach, reporting errors, routing decisions into the template, and objecting that automation made maintenance boring or ruled the image. What varies is building the system, governing it, and reacting to it; the bot's own output is not coded as conduct.

second_order: turning canvas visibility into new people for the subreddit
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants connect the visible canvas work with an influx, discovery of the subreddit, and welcoming those who arrived. What varies is asking what caused the influx, claiming the art caused it, reporting discovery, and greeting the newcomer.

second_order: taking the surviving picture as proof the fandom showed up
theme_note: These codes interpret the picture's presence and survival as evidence about this fandom: people compare it with absent or destroyed Disney figures and say different parts of their own fandom improved the result. What varies is comparison with outsiders versus an internal account of who participated.

second_order: asking to keep the finished art in the subreddit
theme_note: This single-code theme preserves a distinct post-event practice: asking that the completed canvas image become the banner or sidebar. No other code shows whether the request was implemented.

second_order: accounting for whose pixels and effort made it through
theme_note: These codes turn the closed canvas into contribution accounting by asking whether one's pixels survived, describing how effort was allocated, or explaining why someone could not contribute more. What varies is traceability, self-reported allocation, and unrealized willingness to help.

second_order: mapping the friendly neighbours after the canvas closed
theme_note: These codes belong together because the completion post inventories the pictures surrounding Zootopia and calls them friendly neighbours. What varies only by compass direction and named place; the practice is retrospective mapping, not evidence that every named group reciprocated friendship.

second_order: explaining how the picture survived threats and luck
theme_note: These codes offer participant explanations for survival after the fact: an early spot and low visibility are credited as luck, the black void is described as a bandwagon threat, and people recount diverting pixels or tangling with it. What varies is the proposed reason and the response; these are attributed explanations, not independently established causes.

second_order: making room for a newcomer's life beyond the canvas
theme_note: These codes form one side exchange in which an arrival opens into family advice, promised comforting art, and thanks. The practice differs from recruiting or counting subscribers because participants respond to the person's life rather than to the canvas.

second_order: joking about who controls the stickies after r/place
theme_note: These codes enact moderator banter after event pinning clears: a moderator jokes that stickies are whatever they want, another calls it mod despotism, and the moderator answers by offering to pin requests. What varies is boast, mock accusation, and accommodating reply.
